proof:
Source: Simon, Introduction to GMT, Ch. 2 §5, 5.1-5.4 with the printed derivation (pp. 61-63), and §4 (4.11 chain rule for Jacobians). Erratum applied (GMT/Ch02/README.md): for the second variation 5.4 the deformation is assumed of class C³ instead of C² (with C² the acceleration Z is only continuous, div_M Z is undefined, and the expansion 5.2 to O(t³) needs a third derivative). Depends on the sibling children area_formula (area formula 3.4/3.5; the chart versions in SimonGMT WeightedArea.lean may be used equivalently) and submanifold_tangent (T_yM = range Dψ, M Borel, y ↦ P_y continuous on M).

Setting and notation (frozen definitions). n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, N := n + ℓ, ℝ^d = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d). M ⊆ ℝᴺ is an n-dimensional C¹ Simon submanifold, U ⊆ ℝᴺ open, U ∩ M ≠ ∅, μHE[n](K′ ∩ M) < ∞ for every compact K′ ⊆ U, and φ : ℝ → ℝᴺ → ℝᴺ satisfies IsAdmissibleDeformation r U K φ (r = 2 for FirstVariation, r = 3 for SecondVariation): U open, K ⊆ U compact, Φ(t,x) := φ t x is C^r on (−1,1) × U, φ_0 = id on U, φ_t(x) = x for t ∈ (−1,1) and x ∉ K, and for t ∈ (−1,1) φ_t maps U bijectively onto U with fderiv ℝ φ_t x bijective for x ∈ U. X := initialVelocity φ, X(x) = ∂_tΦ(0,x); Z := initialAcceleration φ, Z(x) = ∂²_tΦ(0,x). For y ∈ M: T_y := tangentSpace M y, P_y := tangentProjection M y, τ_i = τ_i(y) := tangentFrame M y (an orthonormal basis of T_y). Hⁿ := μHE[n]. A(t) := deformedArea n M K φ t = (Hⁿ(φ_t(M ∩ K))).toReal. div_M Y(y) := tangentialDivergence M Y y = Σ_i ⟨τ_i, DY(y)τ_i⟩.

PART I. PRINTED DERIVATION (cleaned transcription).
Let X, Z denote the initial velocity and acceleration of φ_t; then (5.2) φ_t(x) = x + tX_x + (t²/2)Z_x + O(t³), and X, Z have compact support in U. Let M_t = φ_t(M ∩ K). The area formula gives Hⁿ(φ_t(M ∩ K)) = ∫_{M∩K} J_t dHⁿ, ψ_t = φ_t|M ∩ U, and hence to compute the first and second variation we can differentiate under the integral; the computation reduces to ∂J_t/∂t and ∂²J_t/∂t² at t = 0. For fixed x, dψ_t|_x(τ) = D_τψ_t = τ + tD_τX + (t²/2)D_τZ + O(t³) (τ ∈ T_xM). Relative to orthonormal bases τ_1,…,τ_n of T_xM and e_1,…,e_{n+ℓ}, dψ_t|_x has i-th row D_{τ_i}ψ_t(x) = τ_i + tD_{τ_i}X + (t²/2)D_{τ_i}Z + O(t³), and (dψ_t|_x)*∘dψ_t|_x has matrix b_ij = δ_ij + t(τ_i·D_{τ_j}X + τ_j·D_{τ_i}X) + t²(½(τ_i·D_{τ_j}Z + τ_j·D_{τ_i}Z) + D_{τ_i}X·D_{τ_j}X) + O(t³). Using det(I + A) = 1 + trace A + ½(trace A)² − ½ trace(A²) + O(|A|³) and √(1+x) = 1 + x/2 − x²/8 + O(x³) one gets J_t = 1 + t div_M X + (t²/2)(div_M Z + (div_M X)² + Σ_i|(D_{τ_i}X)^⊥|² − Σ_{i,j}(τ_i·D_{τ_j}X)(τ_j·D_{τ_i}X)) + O(t³), where (D_{τ_i}X)^⊥ is the normal part. Thus the area formula yields (5.3) d/dt Hⁿ(M_t)|_{t=0} = ∫_M div_M X dHⁿ and (5.4) d²/dt² Hⁿ(M_t)|_{t=0} = ∫_M (div_M Z + (div_M X)² + Σ_i|(D_{τ_i}X)^⊥|² − Σ_{i,j}(τ_i·D_{τ_j}X)(τ_j·D_{τ_i}X)) dHⁿ.

PART II. COMPLETE PROOF OF FirstVariation ∧ SecondVariation.

Step 1 (regularity of the deformation).
1. X is C^{r−1} on ℝᴺ and vanishes on ℝᴺ∖K: on U, X = ∂_tΦ(0,·) is C^{r−1}; on the open set ℝᴺ∖K, Φ(t,x) = x for all t ∈ (−1,1), so X = 0 there; the two open sets cover ℝᴺ (K ⊆ U). For r = 3 likewise Z is C¹ on ℝᴺ and Z = 0 off K. In particular X, DX (and Z, DZ) vanish at every point of ℝᴺ∖K.
2. A_t(x) := D_xΦ(t,x) = fderiv ℝ φ_t x is C^{r−1} in (t,x) on (−1,1) × U, and by symmetry of mixed partial derivatives (Φ ∈ C²) ∂_tA_t(x) = D_x∂_tΦ(t,x), so ∂_tA_t(x)|_{t=0} = DX(x); for r = 3 also ∂²_tA_t(x)|_{t=0} = DZ(x). A_0(x) = I for x ∈ U.
3. For t ∈ (−1,1), φ_t is injective on ℝᴺ (on U by BijOn; φ_t maps U into U and fixes ℝᴺ∖U pointwise since ℝᴺ∖U ⊆ ℝᴺ∖K), A_t(x) is invertible for x ∈ U, and φ_t is C¹ on a neighbourhood of K. On the compact set I₀ × K, I₀ := [−½, ½], the continuous functions (t,x) ↦ A_t(x), ∂_tA_t(x) (and ∂²_tA_t(x) for r = 3) are bounded and uniformly continuous, and the smallest singular value of A_t(x) is bounded below by some s₀ > 0.

Step 2 (area formula for M_t). For y ∈ M ∩ K and t ∈ (−1,1) let L_{t,y} := A_t(y)|_{T_y} : T_y → ℝᴺ and J_t(y) := normDet(L_{t,y}) = √det(L_{t,y}*L_{t,y}); in the orthonormal basis τ_i of T_y, J_t(y)² = det b(t,y), b_ij(t,y) := ⟨A_t(y)τ_i, A_t(y)τ_j⟩ (Gram matrix). Claim: for t ∈ (−1,1), Hⁿ(φ_t(M ∩ K)) = ∫_{M∩K} J_t dHⁿ < ∞, hence A(t) = ∫_{M∩K} J_t dHⁿ.
4. Choose countably many local representations ψ_i : V_i → W_i ∩ M of M (C¹) whose targets W_i cover M (Lindelöf). Put B_i := (M ∩ K ∩ W_i)∖∪_{l<i}W_l (Borel, as M is Borel by submanifold_tangent), pairwise disjoint with union M ∩ K, and B′_i := V_i ∩ ψ_i⁻¹(B_i) (Borel), so ψ_i(B′_i) = B_i.
5. For x ∈ B′_i, ψ_i(x) ∈ K ⊆ U, so φ_t∘ψ_i is differentiable at x with D(φ_t∘ψ_i)(x) = A_t(ψ_i(x))∘Dψ_i(x), which is injective; and φ_t∘ψ_i is injective on B′_i. By the area formula for injective maps with injective derivative (SimonGMT injective_area_formula_areaJacobianAt, or the sibling AreaFormula applied on compact pieces where the map is Lipschitz), Hⁿ(φ_t(B_i)) = ∫_{B′_i} J(φ_t∘ψ_i) dLⁿ.
6. Chain rule for Jacobians (4.11): for linear L : ℝⁿ → ℝᴺ injective and A : ℝᴺ → ℝᴺ, normDet(A∘L) = normDet(L)·normDet(A|_{range L}) (Mathlib LinearMap.normDet_comp; SimonGMT areaJacobian_comp_eq_parametrization_mul_tangential). With L = Dψ_i(x), range L = T_{ψ_i(x)} (submanifold_tangent), so J(φ_t∘ψ_i)(x) = Jψ_i(x)·J_t(ψ_i(x)).
7. By the weighted area formula for the representation ψ_i (SimonGMT IsSimonLocalRepresentation.weighted_area_formula), ∫_{B′_i} Jψ_i·(J_t∘ψ_i) dLⁿ = ∫_{B_i} J_t dHⁿ. Hence Hⁿ(φ_t(B_i)) = ∫_{B_i} J_t dHⁿ. The sets φ_t(B_i) are pairwise disjoint (φ_t injective) and measurable (images of Borel sets under continuous injective maps on Borel sets, e.g. via ContinuousOn.measurableEmbedding as in the library), so summing over i gives the claim. Finiteness: for fixed t ∈ (−1,1), J_t(y) ≤ ‖A_t(y)‖ⁿ ≤ sup_{x∈K}‖A_t(x)‖ⁿ < ∞ (A_t is continuous on the compact K) and Hⁿ(M ∩ K) < ∞ (hypothesis with K′ = K).
8. Basis-free form and measurability: for y ∈ M, J_t(y) = √det(P_y A_t(y)* A_t(y) P_y + (I − P_y)) (determinant on ℝᴺ; block-diagonal with respect to T_y ⊕ T_y^⊥). Since y ↦ P_y is continuous on M (submanifold_tangent) and A_t is continuous, y ↦ J_t(y) and its t-derivatives below are continuous on M ∩ K, hence Hⁿ⌊M-measurable.

Step 3 (pointwise expansion; the printed computation). Fix y ∈ M ∩ K and write A_t = A_t(y), b(t) = b(t,y). b(0) = I and, by Step 1.2,
 ḃ_ij(0) = ⟨DXτ_i, τ_j⟩ + ⟨τ_i, DXτ_j⟩, and for r = 3: b̈_ij(0) = ⟨DZτ_i, τ_j⟩ + ⟨τ_i, DZτ_j⟩ + 2⟨DXτ_i, DXτ_j⟩ (DX = DX(y), DZ = DZ(y)).
9. det b(t) = J_t² > 0 for t ∈ (−1,1) (A_t invertible). Jacobi's formula: (det b)′ = det b·tr(b⁻¹ḃ), so (det b)′(0) = tr ḃ(0) = 2Σ_i⟨τ_i, DXτ_i⟩ = 2 div_M X(y). Hence ∂_tJ_t(y)|_{t=0} = (det b)′(0)/(2√det b(0)) = div_M X(y).
10. (r = 3) Differentiating Jacobi's formula once more at 0 (b(0) = I): (det b)″(0) = tr b̈(0) + (tr ḃ(0))² − tr(ḃ(0)²). Then ∂²_tJ_t|_{t=0} = ½(det b)″(0) − ¼((det b)′(0))² = ½tr b̈(0) + ¼(tr ḃ(0))² − ½tr(ḃ(0)²). With a_ij := ⟨τ_i, DXτ_j⟩: tr b̈(0) = 2div_M Z + 2Σ_i|DXτ_i|², (tr ḃ(0))² = 4(div_M X)², tr(ḃ(0)²) = Σ_{i,j}(a_ij + a_ji)² = 2Σa_ij² + 2Σa_ij a_ji. So ∂²_tJ_t|₀ = div_M Z + (div_M X)² + (Σ_i|DXτ_i|² − Σ_{i,j}a_ji²) − Σ_{i,j}a_ij a_ji, and by Pythagoras |DXτ_i|² = |P_y DXτ_i|² + |(DXτ_i)^⊥|² with |P_yDXτ_i|² = Σ_j⟨τ_j, DXτ_i⟩² = Σ_j a_ji², the bracket equals Σ_i|(DXτ_i)^⊥|², where (v)^⊥ = normalPart M y v = v − P_y v. Since a_ij a_ji = ⟨τ_i, DXτ_j⟩⟨τ_j, DXτ_i⟩, ∂²_tJ_t(y)|_{t=0} = secondVariationIntegrand M φ y exactly (div_M Z + (div_M X)² + Σ_i‖normalPart M y (DX τ_i)‖² − Σ_iΣ_j⟨τ_i, DXτ_j⟩⟨τ_j, DXτ_i⟩).
11. For y ∈ M∖K both integrands of the frozen statement vanish (X, Z, DX, DZ vanish at y by Step 1.1), consistent with ∫_M = ∫_{M∩K}.

Step 4 (differentiation under the integral sign).
12. Uniform bounds: on I₀ × (M ∩ K), det b(t,y) ≥ s₀^{2n} > 0, and b, ∂_tb (and ∂²_tb for r = 3) are bounded and continuous in t uniformly in y (they are polynomial in A_t(y), ∂_tA_t(y), ∂²_tA_t(y) and the unit vectors τ_i(y), and these are uniformly continuous on I₀ × K by Step 1.3). Hence ∂_tJ_t(y) = ∂_t det b/(2√det b) (and ∂²_tJ_t) are bounded on I₀ × (M ∩ K) by a constant and continuous in t uniformly in y.
13. First variation (r = 2): since Hⁿ(M ∩ K) < ∞, constants are integrable on M ∩ K, and Mathlib hasDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_loc_of_deriv_le gives that A is differentiable at 0 with A′(0) = ∫_{M∩K} ∂_tJ_t|₀ dHⁿ = ∫_{M∩K} div_M X dHⁿ = ∫_M div_M X dHⁿ (Step 3.9 and 3.11; integrability: bounded measurable integrand on a finite-measure set, zero off M ∩ K). This is HasDerivAt (deformedArea n M K φ) (∫ y in M, tangentialDivergence M (initialVelocity φ) y ∂μHE[n]) 0, i.e. FirstVariation.
14. Second variation (r = 3): the same theorem applied at every t₀ ∈ (−½, ½) shows that A is differentiable on (−½, ½) with A′(t) = ∫_{M∩K} ∂_tJ_t dHⁿ, so ∀ᶠ t in 𝓝 0, DifferentiableAt ℝ A t and deriv A = A′ on (−½,½). Applying it once more to t ↦ ∫_{M∩K} ∂_tJ_t dHⁿ (domination of ∂²_tJ_t by a constant) gives HasDerivAt (deriv A) (∫_{M∩K} ∂²_tJ_t|₀ dHⁿ) 0, and by Step 3.10-3.11 the value is ∫_M secondVariationIntegrand M φ y dHⁿ. Since deriv A agrees with A′ on a neighbourhood of 0, HasDerivAt (deriv (deformedArea n M K φ)) (∫ y in M, secondVariationIntegrand M φ y ∂μHE[n]) 0. This is SecondVariation.
15. Remarks: the frame τ(y) may be chosen non-continuously; only the basis-independent quantities J_t(y), div_M X(y) = trace(P_y DX(y)), Σ_i|DXτ_i|² = trace(P_y DX(y)* DX(y) P_y), Σ_{i,j}a_ij a_ji = trace((P_y DX(y) P_y)²) and Σ_i|(DXτ_i)^⊥|² = trace(P_y DX(y)*(I − P_y)DX(y)P_y) enter, and these are continuous on M (Step 2.8), which gives the measurability needed in 13-14. The hypothesis (U ∩ M) ≠ ∅ is not used.
key_steps: X, Z are C^{r−1}, C^{r−2} on ℝᴺ and vanish off K; D_xφ_t is jointly continuous with uniformly positive singular values on [−1/2,1/2] × K.
Area formula on charts and the Jacobian chain rule give Hⁿ(φ_t(M ∩ K)) = ∫_{M∩K} J_t dHⁿ with J_t = √det of the Gram matrix of D_xφ_t on T_yM.
Jacobi formula: ∂_tJ_t at 0 is div_M X; ∂²_tJ_t at 0 is exactly the frozen second-variation integrand (Pythagoras for the normal part).
Uniform bounds and finite measure of M ∩ K allow differentiation under the integral (once for 5.3, twice for 5.4); basis-free trace formulas give measurability.
